title: Inferential Capability Does Not Determine Legal Scope
abstract: arXiv:2608.10601v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Two instruments of EU digital law place inference at their centre and mean different things by it. Article 3(1) of the AI Act uses the capability to infer constitutively: it is the central feature separating the regulated category from conventional software. The GDPR never defines inference, yet governs it protectively: the consequences follow from the processing of personal data and from what the inference says about, or does to, a person, whether or not the technology that produced it qualifies as an AI system.   The two perimeters are not concentric. Their non-coincidence remained invisible in single-shot systems; agentic architectures make it operationally acute. The thesis: inferential capability does not determine legal scope, and its absence does not create immunity.   The framework is two-level. Inference performs two legal functions, constitutive and protective; the protective function operates through three pathways -

translated_title: 推理能力并不决定法律范围
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.10601v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：欧盟数字法律的两项工具将推理置于核心位置，但对它的含义有所不同。《人工智能法案》第3条第1款以构成性方式使用推理能力：它是将受监管类别与传统软件区分开来的核心特征。《通用数据保护条例》从未定义推理，却以保护性方式对其进行治理：其后果源于个人数据的处理以及推理对个人所说或所做之事，无论产生该推理的技术是否被归类为人工智能系统。这两个范围并非同心。它们的不重合在单次系统中不可见；而代理架构使其在操作上变得尖锐。论点：推理能力并不决定法律范围，其缺失也不创造豁免权。该框架是双层次的。推理履行两种法律功能，构成性和保护性；保护性功能通过三条路径运作——
tldr: 本文指出欧盟法律中推理能力不决定法律适用范围，其缺失也不豁免责任，并提出了构成性与保护性双重功能框架。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that inferential capability does not determine legal scope under EU law, and its absence does not create immunity, proposing a two-level framework with constitutive and protective functions.
